subsection.title: Avoiding lost or extra solutions
subsection.p: Trigonometric equations invite two common mistakes.
First, dividing by a trigonometric expression can lose solutions.
Second, squaring both sides can introduce extra solutions.

example.title: division can lose solutions
example.p: Do not divide by \cos x. Instead, move all terms to one side:
Blindly dividing by \cos x would leave \sin x=1 and miss the solution x=3\pi/2. Such division is not valid at either solution of the original equation.
